title: Prestige Estates Projects Ltd - 533274 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Prestige Q2 FY27 residential sales rose 20% YoY to INR7,225 crore; H1 sales INR13,804 crore; FY27 booking guidance held at INR36,000 crore.
summary.overview: Management reported a strong first half of FY27, with Q2 residential sales of INR7,225 crore (up 20% YoY) and Q2 revenue from operations of INR2,222 crore. Q2 PAT was INR256 crore and H1 PAT INR527 crore. Collections were INR5,294 crore in Q2 and INR10,096 crore in H1. The CPP Investments deal for the hospitality platform received its first INR1,500 crore tranche in October 2026, and management reiterated FY27 booking guidance of INR36,000 crore alongside a launch pipeline of over INR45,000 crore for the next two years.

financial_highlights.value: INR12,375 per sq ft / INR11,618 per sq ft

segments.name: Residential
segments.commentary: Q2 sales of 5.84 million sq ft and 3,910 units; H1 sales of 11.88 million sq ft and 7,247 units. Bengaluru 41%, Hyderabad 32%, Mumbai 12%, Chennai 8%, others 7%. Completed 4.27 million sq ft in Q2, taking H1 completions to 5 million sq ft.

segments.name: Office
segments.commentary: Leased 1.7 million sq ft in H1; exit rental INR884 crore as of September 2026. Commenced construction on three commercial projects (2 million sq ft) in Chennai and Kochi; completed Prestige Trade Center, Delhi Aerocity (800,000 sq ft).

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Q2 gross turnover INR721 crore (+10% YoY), footfall 5.2 million, occupancy 99%, exit rental INR278 crore. Construction started on Forum One OMR, Chennai (1.39 million sq ft).

segments.name: Hospitality
segments.commentary: H1 occupancy 70%, average room rate INR15,143. Started JW Marriott Sakleshpur and Moxy One OMR Chennai (313 keys, 0.77 million sq ft). CPP Investments committed INR3,000 crore for about 20% of Prestige Hospitality Ventures; INR1,500 crore tranche received in October 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 residential booking value guidance maintained at INR36,000 crore; management said it does not want to over-promise.
FY27 gross collections guided at INR24,000-25,000 crore; operating cash flow about INR9,000 crore; free cash flow about INR9,000 crore.
Construction spend guided at INR10,000-11,000 crore for FY27, with H2 slightly higher due to large launches.
Business development spend guided at INR4,000-5,000 crore for FY27.

H2 FY27 launches of about INR46,000 crore; management said at least INR20,000 crore would launch in Q3 itself. Five projects (Falcon City Thane, Bougainvillea Noida, Avon and Springwood Bengaluru, Sea Scapes Goa) expected in Q3 subject to RERA; Chambers 51 office also in Q3.
DIAL Mumbai hotel keys to be handed to Marriott management on 28 November; bookings expected three to four weeks later. DIAL office rent expected to fully yield by April 2027.
capex_capacity: Pending hotel capex of about INR5,000 crore across ongoing and upcoming hotels; stabilised hotel revenue not yet quantified.
CPP deal: second tranche INR750 crore expected in one year and third INR750 crore after two years; attributable stake to rise from about 16% to 27% after both tranches.

Acquired a retail mall (Forum South 2 per management) for INR590 crore; 930,000 sq ft leasable area, expected to trade in 9-12 months after interiors and tenanting. Average rent assumed about INR130 per sq ft.
Office: BKC X about 2.5 million sq ft with about 1.5 million sq ft leased (leasing paused for top-tier tenants); Chambers 51 about 400,000 sq ft leased; both expected to be completed by end-2027.
Prestige share of unconsolidated JV debt about INR2,400 crore.

Annuity pipeline timelines revised for some upcoming projects due to approval delays; ongoing portfolio construction said to be on schedule. FY31 exit rental raised by about INR250 crore plus from a Raidurg, Hyderabad land parcel moved into the pipeline.
demand_pricing: Management said sales growth came from a general push by sales teams, not schemes; a few near-complete projects offered staged payment plans (for example 75% upfront, 25% at delivery).
Hyderabad: demand depends on micro-market and pricing; management flagged oversupply risk from free FSI policy, while Prestige Golden Grove sold quickly.
Mumbai ticket focus: about INR2 crore and above in MMR; lower price points in other markets.
NCR: Prestige City Indirapuram over 90% sold; Bougainvillea, Meadows and Falcon City to be tested before further NCR land buys.
Falcon City Thane approval received two days before the call; CC and RERA still pending. Management described survey response as phenomenal but cautious.

qa_highlights.question: How will the CPP Investments stake change and when will the balance INR1,500 crore come in?
qa_highlights.answer: Of the INR1,500 crore tranche one, INR950 crore went to the holding company via secondary sale and INR550 crore to PHVL. Balance INR750 crore due in one year and INR750 crore after two years; attributable stake moves from about 16% to 27%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR36,000 crore FY27 guidance conservative given H1 bookings and H2 launches?
qa_highlights.answer: Management will stick to INR36,000 crore and said it could do more if approvals and RERA come through; FY28 guidance to be discussed after FY27 closes.

qa_highlights.question: Why were FY28 and FY29 annuity exit rentals reduced?
qa_highlights.answer: Some upcoming projects had approval delays and revised completion timelines; ongoing projects are on schedule. The FY31 increase reflects the Raidurg land parcel moved into pipeline, adding about INR250 crore plus.

qa_highlights.question: Was Q2 sales strength driven by any schemes?
qa_highlights.answer: No schemes; management said it was a general sales push plus staged payment options on near-complete projects.

qa_highlights.question: What is the H2 launch split and what is the construction spend outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said at least INR20,000 crore of the INR46,000 crore H2 launches comes in Q3. Construction spend guided at INR10,000-11,000 crore for FY27, with Q2's run rate expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What did the retail acquisition cost and how is it reflected?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisition cost INR590 crore (described as INR520 crore plus INR70 crore on the call), paid and reflected in the September 30 balance sheet.

risks_watch: Launch timing depends on RERA approvals; five Q3 projects and Falcon City Thane are not yet RERA-approved.
Hyderabad and certain micro-markets may face oversupply from free FSI policy.
Annuity ramp-up in FY28-FY29 has been pushed out on some upcoming projects due to approval delays.
Collections and cash flow guidance depends on H2 launches converting into sales.
Hotel pending capex of about INR5,000 crore and the timing of the second and third CPP tranches.
Mall acquisition needs about 9-12 months of fit-out and tenanting before trading; leasing at BKC X paused for top-tier tenants.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the FY27 launch calendar, but cautious on timing: management repeatedly tied launches to RERA approvals and declined to raise the INR36,000 crore booking guidance or give FY28 numbers. Answers on revenue and stake-change details were brief, and the hotel revenue question was deferred.
key_quotes: We do not want to overpromise, underdeliver.
As a policy, we do not believe in schemes because those only give agony in the end.
Right now, it is close to 16%, and once both the tranches are received, we move to 27%.
We will stick to our INR36,000 crores.

growth.why: FY27 booking guidance held at INR36,000 crore (H1 residential sales INR13,804 crore, Q2 +20% YoY) with H2 launches of about INR46,000 crore, at least INR20,000 crore in Q3 subject to RERA approvals; management did not give a revenue growth figure and some annuity timelines were revised for approval delays.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hotels (313 keys, 0.77M sq ft), 3 offices (2M sq ft) and Forum One OMR (1.39M sq ft) are under construction; BKC X (2.5M sq ft) and Chambers 51 complete by end-2027, and the Forum South 2 mall (930,000 sq ft) trades 9-12 months after acquisition.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 residential sales of INR13,804 crore (Q2 +20% YoY, 5.84M sq ft) and at least INR20,000 crore of the INR46,000 crore H2 launches in Q3, though RERA approvals gate timing.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Pending hotel capex of about INR5,000 crore and construction spend of INR10,000-11,000 crore for FY27 indicate sustained new project commitments, and the NCR land buys are on hold until Bougainvillea, Meadows and Falcon City are tested.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management held INR36,000 crore booking guidance and said it could do more if approvals and RERA come through, but declined to raise it on the call.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Collections and cash flow guidance depend on H2 launches converting, and five Q3 projects plus Falcon City Thane still lack RERA approval; some annuity timelines were already pushed out.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: At least INR20,000 crore of H2 launches in Q3 across Falcon City Thane, Bougainvillea Noida, Avon and Springwood Bengaluru, Sea Scapes Goa and Chambers 51 office, subject to RERA.

rows.label: H2 FY27 launch pipeline of about INR46,000 crore
rows.why: At least INR20,000 crore launches in Q3 with H2 totalling about INR46,000 crore, supporting the INR36,000 crore FY27 booking guide, though it depends on RERA.

rows.label: CPP Investments hospitality tranches
rows.when: Q3 FY27 (received); second tranche in one year, third after two years
rows.why: INR1,500 crore first tranche received in October 2026, with INR750 crore due in one year and INR750 crore after two years; attributable stake rises from about 16% to 27%.

rows.label: Mumbai luxury focus (INR2 crore+ in MMR)
rows.why: Management is pushing INR2 crore-plus tickets in MMR while lower price points are used elsewhere, and Mumbai was 12% of Q2 sales mix.

tone.note: Management was confident on H1 sales momentum and the FY27 launch calendar but cautious on RERA-linked timing, declined to raise the INR36,000 crore guide, and deferred the hotel revenue question; analysts pushed on guidance conservatism, the FY28-29 annuity cuts and the CPP stake change.
